sec-head.p: Hands-on builds matched to your retrieval and orchestration needs, with real benchmarks on speed, memory, and hybrid production architectures for 2026.

card.p: An independent architecture assessment of your use case, data, and latency/memory constraints, producing a written recommendation: LangGraph, LlamaIndex, or a hybrid, with benchmark-driven reasoning.
Retrieval-first builds using hierarchical indices, auto-merging retrieval, and query synthesis – delivering 10-25% better multi-source accuracy with lower memory overhead for document-heavy corpora.
Multi-step agent systems with LangGraph graphs: tool use, stateful memory, checkpointing, and human-in-the-loop – for AI that acts, with controlled memory overhead and sub-second graph transitions.
LlamaIndex as the retrieval layer wrapped as a tool inside a LangGraph agent – combining best-in-class hierarchical retrieval with production-grade orchestration and observability in one system.
Assessment and migration for teams hitting friction: adding agentic capability to retrieval-only systems or switching to hybrid to reduce latency and memory bloat.

card cta-card.p: Try the fit-check widget above, or get it scoped properly.

ul: Retrieval quality is the primary bottleneck, not orchestration complexity – hierarchical indices reduce memory overhead by ~30% vs. naive chunking in LangChain.
Complex multi-document reasoning: tree index and response synthesizers produce 10-15% better answers on multi-source synthesis benchmarks with lower retrieval latency.
Your documents are hierarchically structured (legal, code, technical manuals): composable indices deliver 15-25% better answer accuracy with predictable memory usage.
You want to ship faster with less code and lower latency overhead – LlamaIndex's built-in query engines avoid the graph overhead of LangGraph for pure RAG.

card.h3: RAG is one piece of a larger agent
ul: RAG is one component of a larger agentic system, not the whole product – LangGraph's multi-step graphs handle branching and loops with sub-100ms state transitions.
You need tool use, multi-step reasoning, or persistent memory across a conversation – LangGraph's checkpointing adds minimal overhead compared to custom state machines.
Human-in-the-loop checkpoints matter: LangGraph has native interrupt/resume support with serializable state, enabling audit trails without bloating memory.
First-party observability (LangSmith) is a requirement – it provides latency breakdowns per graph node, essential for debugging hybrid architectures.
